business_patterns.top_pattern: Auth and facility classification issues are masking the real spend story
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group / PPO and HMO / Not Mapped facilities and authorization coding

providers: SSM HEALTH SAINT MARY'S HOSPITAL - JEFFERSON CITY

key_driver_codes: AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION
Not Mapped
PPO
HMO
business_patterns.pattern_details: A large share of the increase sits in claims tied to Not Mapped facilities and shifts in authorization coding, especially in OH PPO. Similar but smaller issues also appear in CA, CO, MO, NY, and WI. Until facility and auth classification are corrected, utilization, site-of-care, and reimbursement actions could target the wrong root cause.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the biggest theme in the analysis and it is a gating issue before broader operational action.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Have UM operations and data quality jointly reconcile Not Mapped facility claims and authorization code distribution changes first, then rerun market and product actions only after the classifications are confirmed.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is materially concentrated in Not Mapped facility values and authorization code distribution shifts, so business action should wait until classification and mapping are validated.
evidence_summary: OH PPO Not Mapped facility claims added +$7.4M; the PA=Y slice alone contributed +$5.9M with 44 more admissions and about $95K higher paid per admit.
OH authorization code distribution shifts added another +$1.9M with no trusted volume or unit-cost read until coding is validated.
Additional Not Mapped spend appears in CA at about +$0.7M across PPO and HMO and in CO at +$0.5M for PPO.
MO / NY / WI also show +$0.5M tied to authorization code distribution shifts, reinforcing this as a recurring validation issue.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA spend is concentrated in complex inpatient cases at a small set of hospitals
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / Commercial Local Group / Acute Hospital and complex inpatient case mix
key_driver_codes: Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with CC
Extensive O.R. Procedures Unrelated to Principal Diagnosis with MCC
Pulmonary Embolism with MCC or Acute Cor Pulmonale
HARBORVIEW MEDICAL CENTER
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA shows a concentrated inpatient cost pattern rather than a broad statewide trend. Spend is clustered in complex cardiothoracic, vascular, digestive, and pulmonary embolism cases, with additional pressure tied to PPO acute hospital admissions and a small number of hospitals, especially Harborview Medical Center and UC Irvine Medical Center. The mix includes both rare catastrophic cases and recurring higher-cost admissions.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is one of the largest actionable market patterns and it is concentrated enough to support targeted provider, clinical, and UM intervention.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a joint CA review across Harborview Medical Center and UC Irvine Medical Center to confirm severity, level of care, and reimbursement for cardiothoracic, vascular, digestive, and pulmonary embolism admissions before broader policy changes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: A meaningful share of the CA increase comes from low-volume, high-severity inpatient cases, so severity and claim classification should be confirmed alongside provider economics review.
evidence_summary: CA rare high-cost unclassified cases added +$5.4M, including about +$1.0M from thoracoabdominal aneurysm surgery and +$0.5M from infective endocarditis-related cardiothoracic care.
CA PPO acute hospital admissions added +$1.4M; cardiothoracic cases contributed about +$1.0M across 5 more admissions.
Harborview Medical Center contributed about +$0.3M in CA PPO acute hospital pressure, while UC Irvine Medical Center is repeatedly present in CA high-cost case activity.
Additional CA clinical signals include mitral insufficiency at +$0.4M and pulmonary embolism intensity/reimbursement pressure at +$0.2M.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Secondary-state acute hospital pressure is spreading across products and providers
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group / Acute Hospital and Children's / PPO, POS, and EPO

providers: SSM HEALTH SAINT MARY'S HOSPITAL - JEFFERSON CITY

key_driver_codes: Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with CC
Major Chest Procedures with CC
Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: Outside the largest markets, the analysis shows a repeatable acute hospital pressure pattern across several smaller state segments rather than one isolated event. The same inpatient pathways recur across PPO, POS, and EPO, with some markets driven by more admissions and others by sharply higher paid per admit. The pattern points to a broad provider-mix and utilization issue that can be addressed with a common cross-market playbook.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: The combined impact is large and recurring, making this a scalable operational and reimbursement opportunity.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Stand up a cross-market review for repeated cardiothoracic, chest, digestive, pulmonary embolism, and postpartum admissions in VA, MO, CT, NY, and GA/WI, pairing UM review of admission growth with reimbursement review where paid per admit jumped.
evidence_summary: These secondary-state operational segments combined added about +$5.9M across IN / VA, MO, CT, NY, GA / WI, CA / KY / NY, CA / KY, and VA.
IN / VA PPO acute hospital unit-cost pressure added +$0.9M, led by VA cardiothoracic cases with about +$205K higher paid per admit and flat admissions.
MO PPO acute hospital mixed pressure added +$0.8M, and CT PPO mixed pressure added +$0.7M across repeated chest and digestive admissions.
GA / WI POS added +$0.6M, CA / KY / NY PPO utilization added +$0.5M, and VA POS utilization added +$0.4M, showing the issue is recurring across products and segments.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CO inpatient costs are rising even as admissions soften
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CO / Commercial Local Group / Acute Hospital, Children's, and Critical Access
key_driver_codes: PPO
EPO
ACUTE HOSPITAL
CRITICAL ACCESS
business_patterns.pattern_details: CO is showing a clear reimbursement and unit-cost problem rather than broad utilization growth. Both PPO and EPO acute hospital segments rose while admissions fell, and smaller spillover also appears in Children's and Critical Access facilities. This points to higher paid amounts per stay across multiple CO inpatient settings.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A price-led inpatient trend can compound quickly and calls for a different response than admission management alone.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Reprice recent CO inpatient claims and compare contract performance across PPO and EPO acute hospital admissions first, then extend the review to Children's and Critical Access claims where the same pattern is emerging.
evidence_summary: CO PPO acute hospital spend rose +$1.4M even with 4 fewer admissions; paid per admit increased by about $8K.
CO EPO acute hospital spend rose +$1.1M with 4 fewer admissions; paid per admit increased by about $30K.
CO Children's added +$0.2M and CO Critical Access added +$0.2M, showing the unit-cost issue is not limited to one facility type.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NY-centered thoracic and maternal complications are emerging as focused case-mix pressure
key_driver_codes: Major Chest Procedures with CC
Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with CC
Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
SEVERE PRE-ECLAMP COMP PUERPERIUM
business_patterns.pattern_details: NY is showing a focused mix of high-cost thoracic and pulmonary episodes along with maternal complications, rather than a broad inpatient trend. The CA / NY segment adds related valve, lung, and puerperium cases, reinforcing that these are concentrated episode types with different care pathways. This pattern should be handled through targeted clinical review, not broad product action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small numbers of thoracic and maternal complications can create large swings and need different management responses.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run separate clinical review lanes for thoracic and pulmonary embolism episodes versus postpartum hypertensive complications in NY and CA / NY, and confirm admission severity and episode management opportunities for each lane.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Several of these cases are low-volume and clinically heterogeneous, so severity and case classification should be confirmed before scaling interventions.
evidence_summary: NY rare chest, pleural, pulmonary embolism, and lung cases added +$1.5M across focused episode types.
NY severe pre-eclampsia complicating puerperium added +$0.3M with 13 more admissions.
The CA / NY segment added +$1.1M, including about +$0.6M from nonrheumatic aortic valve disease, +$0.4M from lung cancer-related chest procedures, and a smaller puerperium signal.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic cases are driving a distinct CO / MO / UNATTRIBUTED / WI spike

providers: SSM HEALTH SAINT MARY'S HOSPITAL - JEFFERSON CITY

key_driver_codes: Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System without MCC
Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell and Other Immunotherapies
Disorders of Pancreas Except Malignancy with CC
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: This segment is being driven by a small number of catastrophic and specialty inpatient cases, not by a broad change in utilization. The standout cases include heart transplant or heart assist system admissions, CAR-T and other immunotherapy, and smaller one-off bowel, spinal, respiratory, and cellulitis cases. These episodes are too infrequent to treat as a stable trend without case-level validation.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: One or two catastrophic admissions can create multimillion-dollar swings and can easily be mistaken for a persistent market problem.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send these cases to focused clinical and data-quality review to confirm severity, coding, and claim handling before using them to change broader management or pricing strategy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is dominated by low-baseline, small-number catastrophic cases that require case-level validation before extrapolation.
evidence_summary: CO heart transplant or heart assist system cases added +$1.5M from 1 admission.
CO CAR-T and other immunotherapy added +$0.9M from 1 admission.
The remaining +$0.4M is spread across smaller one-off bowel, spinal, respiratory, and cellulitis cases in MO, WI, UNATTRIBUTED, and CO.

business_patterns.top_pattern: OH PPO acute hospital growth is being driven mainly by more admissions
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH / Commercial Local Group / PPO / Acute Hospital
key_driver_codes: PPO
ACUTE HOSPITAL
Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with CC
Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: Within mapped OH PPO acute hospital claims, the increase is primarily a utilization story. One segment is clearly volume-led, and another shows a mix of more admissions and higher spend, with cardiothoracic cases dominating the pattern. This is an admission-growth issue more than a pricing issue.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: When the increase is mostly admissions-driven, UM and pathway controls are the most direct lever.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit OH PPO acute hospital admission growth under authorization, starting with cardiothoracic and postpartum pathways, and tighten pre-service management if admission criteria or routing changed.
evidence_summary: OH PPO acute hospital utilization added +$1.2M with 36 more admissions while paid per admit was essentially flat to down.
A second OH PPO acute hospital pattern added +$0.8M, including about +$0.7M from cardiothoracic admissions across 4 more stays.
The repeated PA=Y signal suggests the first lever is admission management, not broad reimbursement action.

business_patterns.top_pattern: HMO acute hospital pressure is recurring across CA / CO / NH / OH
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / CO / NH / OH / Commercial Local Group / HMO / Acute Hospital
key_driver_codes: HMO
ACUTE HOSPITAL
Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with CC
Pulmonary Embolism with MCC or Acute Cor Pulmonale
business_patterns.pattern_details: The HMO acute hospital segment shows a repeat pattern of both admission growth and higher paid amounts per stay across CA, CO, NH, and OH. The biggest signals come from OH authorized admissions and CA cardiothoracic cases, with smaller contributions from pulmonary embolism and provider concentration in CO. This is a recurring product-and-setting pattern rather than a one-off outlier.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Because the same product and facility combination repeats across several states, a standardized HMO action can have broad impact.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Compare HMO authorization rules and reimbursement outcomes for acute hospital cardiothoracic and pulmonary embolism admissions across CA, OH, CO, and NH, then standardize any avoidable market differences.
evidence_summary: The CA / CO / NH / OH HMO acute hospital segment added +$1.9M overall.
OH PA=Y HMO acute hospital admissions contributed about +$0.8M with 3 more admissions and roughly $86K higher paid per admit.
CA non-PA HMO cardiothoracic admissions contributed about +$0.8M across 3 admissions at roughly $272K higher paid per admit.
Smaller contributions came from NH pulmonary embolism and CO provider concentration at UCHealth Yampa Valley Medical Center.

executive_summary.headline: The biggest cost themes are validation-first auth and facility classification issues, CA provider-concentrated complex inpatient cases, and recurring acute hospital pressure across multiple commercial segments.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Authorization coding shifts and Not Mapped facilities account for the largest increase and should be validated before broad action. After that, the highest-value opportunities are concentrated inpatient case review in CA, reimbursement pressure in CO, and a repeatable acute hospital admission and unit-cost playbook across smaller state segments and HMO markets.
recommended_focus_order: Validate authorization code distribution and Not Mapped facility classification before acting on apparent trend lines.
Target CA and CO inpatient concentration next, with joint clinical, UM, and reimbursement review on complex and high-cost admissions.
Apply a cross-market acute hospital playbook to recurring PPO, POS, EPO, and HMO segments once validation is complete.

notes: All 30 analytical groups were assigned to one business pattern without reusing groups.
Validation issues were consolidated into one gating pattern to avoid mixing data-quality noise with operational action.
